out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' PIC WAS UNABLE TO PROVIDE EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY DURING INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. CDI: EH POLICY PROVIDED VIA EMAIL. PRINT ONE OUT FOR EACH EMPLOYEE, HAVE EACH EMPLOYEE SIGN ONE, AND KEEP THEM ONSITE AT ALL TIMES FOR REVIEW.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. CDI: CLEAN-UP FORM PROVIDED DURING INSPECTION. YOU MUST KEEP ONSITE AT ALL TIMES FOR REVIEW.

out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Approved Record Keeping, Tags/Labels
violations.observation: A record keeping system is not in place to maintain the tags of used/sold shellstock in chronological order correlated to the date that is recorded on the tag/label. OBSERVED THE TAGS TO BE DISORGANIZED AND STUFFED INTO A PLASTIC BOX.
violations.corrective_action: Tags/labels must be maintained in chronological order by the date recorded on the tag/label when the last shellstock is used/sold. TAGS FROM THE LAST THREE MONTHS MUST BE PUT IN CHRONOLOGICAL ORDER BY JUNE 23RD. YOU MAY DISPOSE OF TAGS THAT ARE OLDER THAN 3 MONTHS OLD.

violations.title: Shellstock Removed from Tagged or Labeled Container
violations.observation: Shellstock has been removed from the tagged/labeled container without preserving source identification. OBSERVED SHELLSTOCK IN THE WALK-IN COOLER WITHOUT THE TAG.
violations.corrective_action: Shellstock that has been removed from the tagged/labeled container must have a system used to identify source. CDI: PIC PUT TAG WITH THE SHELLSTOCK AT TIME OF INSPECTION. YOU MUST MAKE COPIES OF THE TAG AND KEEP WITH EACH PIECE OF SHELLSTOCK.

violations.title: Shellstock Label Marked, Last Date Served/Sold Info
violations.observation: The date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served is not recorded on the tag or label.
violations.corrective_action: The identity of the source of shellstock (oysters, clams, mussels) that are sold or served shall be maintained by retaining shellstock tags or labels and marking the tag or label with the date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served. CDI: PIC WAS RE-EDUCATED. THIS MUST BE DONE ON A DAILY BASIS, THE MANAGER MUST ENSURE THE TAGS ARE MARKED AS INDICATED ABOVE.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: OBSERVED RAW SHRIMP STORED ABOVE MARINARA IN THE WALK-IN COOLER.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CDI: SHRIMP MOVED TO THE BOTTOM OF THE COOLER AT TIME OF INSPECTION. CRAZY CRAB (Inspection Date: 06/13/2026) Page 2 of 6

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: OBSERVED IN (1): RAW OYSTERS AT 55F (1HR) OBSERVED IN (3): CUT SAUSAGE AT 55F (1HR)
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: PUT IN FREEZER/FREEZER OPENED TO WIC TO RAPID COOL. PIC RE-EDUCATED ON PROPER COLD-HOLDING TCS FOODS.

violations.observation: Pesticides labeled for residential use were observed in the facility and are being applied by the operator to control pests. OBSERVED RAID FLY BAIT ON A SHELF NEAR THE COOKLINE.
violations.corrective_action: Remove residential use pesticides from the facility. When necessary for pest control, chemical pesticides must be applied by a certified pesticide applicator to prevent injury and contamination. CDI: RAID DISPOSED OF. PIC RE-EDUCATED.

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. OBSERVED CHEMICAL LUBRICANT STORED WITH SINGLE-USE UTENSILS BY THE COOKLINE. OBSERVED WINDEX STORED WITH CLEAN DISHES IN TWO LOCATIONS. OBSERVED HANDSOAP STORED WITH ALCOHOL IN THE OFFICE. OBSERVED BATHROOM CLEANER STORED NEXT TO THE TO GO BOXES AND A SPICE BIN.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. CDI: ALL CHEMICALS WERE PROPERLY LOCATED DURING INSPECTION. PIC WAS RE-EDUCATED.

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. OBSERVED MULTIPLE SQUIRT BOTTLES OF CHEMICALS WITHOUT LABELS. THESE WERE SCATTERED THROUGHOUT THE FACILITY.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. ALL CONTAINERS OF CHEMICALS MUST BE LABELED WITH THEIR COMMON NAME BY JUNE 23RD. CRAZY CRAB (Inspection Date: 06/13/2026) Page 3 of 6

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: OBSERVED COOKED CHICKEN AT DEEP FRYERS “COOLING” AT ROOM TEMPERATURE STACKED THICKLY ON BAKING SHEETS. OBSERVED COOKED POTATOES ON BACK COUNTER “COOLING” STACKED THICKLY IN DEEP BINS.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI: FOOD SPREAD OUT THINLY ON MULTIPLE BAKING SHEETS AND PLACED IN FREEZER. PIC RE-EDUCATED.

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: OBSERVED AT LEAST ONE DOZEN DEEP BINS OF COOKED CORN “COOLING” IN THE WIC STACKED ON TOP OF EACH OTHER AND THICKLY LAYERED IN EACH BIN. OBSERVED COOKED POTATOES AND COOKED CORN STORED IN DEEP BINS, DEEPLY LAYERED IN THE PEPSI FRIDGE.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI: PIC RE-EDUCATED. FOOD REARRANGED AND PLACED IN FREEZER TO RAPID COOL.

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.title: Thermometers, Location in Holding Units
violations.observation: The temperature measuring device in the following mechanically refrigerated unit was not properly located in the warmest part of the unit: OBSERVED THE THERMOMETERS IN MOST COOLERS TO BE STORED IN THE BACK OF THE COOLERS.
violations.corrective_action: In a mechanically refrigerated unit the sensor of a temperature measuring device shall be located to measure the air temperature of a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of the refrigerator. Store the thermometer near the door of the unit. CDI: PIC RE-EDUCATED. THERMOMETERS RELOCATED TO THE FRONT OF THE UNITS.

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. OBSERVED FOOD, BEER, AND POP STORED ON THE FLOOR THROUGHOUT THE FACILITY INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO IN THE WALK-IN FREEZER, IN THE OFFICE, BEHIND THE BAR, AND NEAR THE COOKLINE.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: OBSERVED A RICE SCOOP STORED IN TEPID WATER. OBSERVED MULTIPLE SINGLE USE BOWLS INSIDE OF DRY FOODS AND DRY SPICES.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. ALL IN USE UTENSILS MUST BE STORED PROPERLY. YOU MUST PURCHASE SCOOPS AND THE HANDLES MUST BE UP AND OUT OF THE FOOD. THIS MUST BE CORRECTED BY JUNE 23RD. CRAZY CRAB (Inspection Date: 06/13/2026) Page 4 of 6

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: OBSERVED THE WALK-IN COOLER TO BE AT ~52F AND HOLDING FOOD FROM 40-80F. OBSERVED THE ONE-DOOR STANDING PEPSI COOLER TO BE AT 61F AND HOLDING FOOD ~52F. OBSERVED THE TWO-DOOR UNDER COUNTER COOLER TO BE AT 56F. OBSERVED THE TWO-DOOR PREP-TOP COOLER ACROSS FROM THE COOKLINE TO BE NON FUNCTIONAL.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. THE WALK-IN FREEZER DOOR WAS OPENED TO PROPERLY COOL DOWN THE WALK-IN COOLER. REAPIR TECHNICIAN WAS CALLED DURING INSPECTION. ALL OF THE ABOVE COOLERS MUST BE FIXED/ADJUSTED TO HOLD FOOD AT 41F OR BELOW. DUE TO THE AMOUNT OF COOLING YOU REQUIRE, I RECOMMEND SETTING COOLERS TO AROUND 33-35F AT MOST. YOU MUST MONITOR THE TEMPERATURES OF THE FOOD INSIDE THE UNITS ON A REGULAR BASIS. DO NOT STORE ANY TCS FOOD ITEMS IN ANY OF THE AFFECTED COOLERS BESIDES THE WALK-IN COOLER WITH THE FREEZER DOOR OPEN. THIS MUST BE CORRECTED BY JUNE 23RD.
